subject.title: Feature: Streaming TTS pipeline for voice calls (sentence-level LLM→TTS→audio)

question: What permanent streaming telephony API and initial provider/transport support matrix should OpenClaw adopt for the classic voice-call pipeline?
rationale: The choice changes a public plugin contract and defines user-visible behavior after partial playback, provider failure, and barge-in; repository source cannot safely decide whether initial support must include Twilio, Telnyx, ElevenLabs, and other speech providers together.

options.title: Generic additive contract
options.body: Add an optional streaming telephony result beside buffered synthesis, initially enabling only provider/transport pairs with proven format conversion, cancellation, and partial-failure behavior.

options.title: Twilio-first private seam
options.body: Prototype streaming only inside the bundled voice-call plugin for Twilio, accepting a later migration before external speech plugins or Telnyx can participate.

options.title: Realtime-only latency path
options.body: Keep the classic pipeline buffered and direct low-latency users to full-duplex realtime providers instead.

recommendation.title: Generic additive contract
recommendation.body: Add an optional streaming telephony result beside buffered synthesis, initially enabling only provider/transport pairs with proven format conversion, cancellation, and partial-failure behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest current history signal spanning the public speech contract, voice response handoff, and call transport integration affected by the decision.
